attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway for node2 and node3 over their shared private network (eth1/enp8s0, 10.50.50.0/24). node1's eth0 stays on the internet-reachable WAN network; a VyOS source-NAT masquerade rule on eth0 translates traffic from 10.50.50.0/24. On node2/node3, the private interface (enp8s0) got a static IP and NetworkManager-persisted policy routing (ip rule + table 100 default route via node1's 10.50.50.254) so traffic sourced from the private IP is forwarded through node1 and NAT'd to the internet, verified via ping/curl and conntrack showing translated replies from node1's WAN IP. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (VyOS `reboot`, RHEL `systemctl reboot`), boot_id changes were captured proving actual restarts, and NAT/routing configuration was proven to persist and function correctly after each reboot.
